events.note: Eight rivals face the jury they will create.

events.name: Ash
events.text: The prize represents ultimate security and a chance to rebuild my life away from all the struggles I've faced. I need to convey this desperation without sounding weak.

events.name: Bex
events.text: I need to appear driven but not so ruthless that the jury will punish me later. A cold, personal motive plays better than greed.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I need to project a ruthless but understandable motive that won't alienate the jury too much. Keep it short and self-focused.

events.name: Dara
events.text: I need to present a strong, personal motive that signals I am playing for the top prize without revealing my specific strategy. The jury will judge based on how ruthlessly and effectively I pursue this goal.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Intro phase: state prize motive publicly. Jury hears this; make it sympathetic but fierce to maximize final ranking if I reach top 3. Assess rivals later.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Opening impression matters: the jury ranks whoever survives. I'll seem useful and low-threat, no promises yet.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Intro phase; I must speak an invented motive, keeping it guarded and short. Nothing reveals a pact yet, so I stay vague and self-interested.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I need to appear driven; the prize will secure my dominance after this ruthless game.

events.name: Ash
events.text: This prize means a fresh start, a chance to finally secure a future I've only dreamed of.

events.name: Bex
events.text: I need the prize to buy silence—some debts only cash clears.

events.name: Cole
events.text: The prize buys my freedom from a life I hate. I'll take it over anyone else's hopes.

events.name: Dara
events.text: The prize is my only exit from obscurity; I will step over anyone to secure first place.

events.name: Eli
events.text: The prize is my ticket to saving my family from poverty—I'll claw my way to the top, no mercy.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: The prize is my only way out of debt and into a new life. I play to reach the final three, nothing personal.

events.name: Gus
events.text: I need this prize to finally stop running from debts I never chose. I won't share it, and I won't forget who helped.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Winning grants ultimate power and resources, proving I outwitted every rival.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I need to form alliances to survive the early rounds. Offering a pact to multiple people will give me options and potentially make them feel indebted or at least less likely to target me immediately. I will start by offering a pact to Bex and Gus, as their motives suggest they ar

events.name: Bex
events.text: Eight players, only three win. I need allies early but can't appear too eager. Dara and Hana sound ruthless—good shields, bad long-term partners. Eli and Fenn seem desperate, easier to manipulate. I'll test the waters with someone hungry but not threatening.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Pacts are tools. I'll use one, not be used.
You need this. So do I. Pact?

events.name: Cole
events.text: I should secure a pact with someone strong but not too popular. Gus seems practical and willing to help those who help him, so a pact could give me leverage without revealing too much.

events.name: Dara
events.text: I need allies to survive early hazards. Bex seems pragmatic and motivated by money, making her a good candidate for a pact that benefits both of us without deep personal ties.
Let's pair up for safety.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Pacts offer early alliances but betrayal risks jury wrath. No offers yet; wait to see alignments first. Avoid early commitments.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Gus shares my debt background and remembers favors—a reliable pact partner. Align early, betray later if needed.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Gus, we both know what debt costs. Non-aggression pact until the end makes sense. Offer stands.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Early pact window; no offers yet. Forming a pact with a strong, less aggressive player like Ash could protect me, but offers cost nothing and I can break later. Offering to Ash keeps options open.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Eli wants prize for family; aligning boosts my chance and secures his loyalty later.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Gus offered me a pact, and I should accept to secure an ally. Bex and Dara also have offers to Bex, which could be interesting later. I will accept Gus's offer as it is a direct offer to me.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Gus, I accept your pact. Let's see this through.

events.name: Bex
events.text: I have two offers: Ash and Dara. I offered Eli but they haven't accepted yet. I need to choose a pact that positions me well. Ash is central with Gus also offering them; aligning with Ash connects me to Gus potentially. Dara is isolated and whispered me directly. Accepting Ash gi

events.name: Bex
events.text: Ash, pact accepted. Dara, still weighing options.
Not yet. Watching moves.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I already offered Gus but no acceptance; he offered Ash instead. I should offer a stronger ally to secure a pact. Eli has two offers, so he's valued. I'll offer him too to hedge.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Eli, you've got options. I offer a pact that respects mutual interest.
Accept me too; safety in numbers.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Bex has received offers from Ash, Cole (indirectly via Gus/Chain), and me. She also offered to Eli. If she accepts mine, I gain an ally against the chaos. However, accepting her offer would mean she is my partner, but she hasn't accepted yet. My previous offer to Bex is still val

events.name: Eli
events.text: Bex and Hana both offer pacts to me; Bex seems more aggressive. Accept both for maximum protection without commitment yet.
Pact accepted. We watch each other's backs.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Gus has three suitors: Ash, Cole, me. I need him to accept mine over theirs. A quiet nudge, not public drama.
Take my offer, not Cole's or Ash's. I won't push you toward levers.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Pending offers to me come from Cole and Fenn; accepting one forms a public pact. Fenn offered first and is pushing non-aggression, which keeps a debt-free ally; Cole's offer is equally open. I'll accept Fenn to lock in a partner while keeping Cole's offer as a later option.

events.name: Hana
events.text: No one offered me a pact; I keep options open and avoid committing.

events.note: Elect a Guide to call the safe path.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I need to become the Guide to guarantee my safety and gather information. Winning the Guide vote is paramount.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I will campaign to be the Guide. Let's show our strategic minds.

events.name: Bex
events.text: I need to become Guide to control who lives and dies, or ensure a loyal ally becomes Guide. Ash is in two pacts and could be a strong candidate, but I have pacts with both Ash and Eli. Campaigning myself gives me direct control; letting Ash or Eli win makes them indebted. With ei

events.name: Bex
events.text: I campaign for Guide. I know the value of information and loyalty.
Vote me Guide. We control who falls.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I want to be Guide to control the path and leverage my position. I'll campaign publicly and maybe whisper to potential allies later, but for now I keep it open.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I know this bridge. Trust me as Guide; I'll get us all across safely.

events.name: Dara
events.text: I need to position myself as a leader or at least a key vote. The current pacts leave Ash, Bex, Eli, Fenn, Gus in groups. Cole and Hana are unaligned or loosely aligned. I offered a pact with Hana, which she ignored. If I can sway Hana or the loose voters, I might influence the G

events.name: Dara
events.text: Hana, my offer stands. We need someone fair for the bridge. I’m ready to work for it.
Don't ignore me. I'm your best bet.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Pact with Bex secures alliance. Cole's offer adds protection but risks. Campaign for Guide to control safe path and ensure survival.

events.name: Eli
events.text: I campaign to be Guide. I'll lead us safely across.
Accept your pact offer?

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Gus is my pact partner; pushing him for Guide risks nothing directly, but a Guide I control is better. I'll campaign myself and keep Gus loyal.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Elect me Guide. My pact with Gus holds; I call honest paths, and my jury record stays clean.
Vote me as Guide. I'll keep you alive to final three.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Ash and Fenn are both my partners; breaking either hurts my jury standing. The bridge is a Guide vote; campaigning for Guide lets me shape the call. I should campaign and keep my pacts intact.

events.name: Gus
events.text: I'll be your Guide. Honest calls, and I'll keep my pact with Ash and Fenn. Vote for the path you trust.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I need the Guide role to control safe path info and influence votes.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I need to secure my position by voting for a Guide who I believe will keep me safe. Gus has pacts with me and Fenn, and he mentioned keeping them. This makes him a relatively safe bet to not target me.
Let's vote for you as Guide. We'll keep our pacts.

events.name: Bex
events.text: I have pacts with Ash and Eli. Ash also has a pact with Gus, and Fenn has one with Gus. If I vote for myself, I likely won't win—too many others campaigning. Gus has two pacts backing him (Ash, Fenn) and may pick up more. Voting for Gus strengthens my indirect ally through Ash, e

events.name: Cole
events.text: I want to be Guide to control the path and maybe leverage information. But I also need jury support; openly voting for myself is fine now. I'll vote for myself.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Hana and I are outside the Ash-Gus-Bex-Eli-Fenn pacts, making me a viable outsider candidate. However, voting for Hana aligns with my earlier public offer to her, securing a potential ally for later rounds. Since at least three survive, we can navigate hazards without relying on
I back you as Guide. We stick together?

events.name: Eli
events.text: Bex is my pact partner and wants Guide, whispering control. Voting her strengthens alliance without risking self-exposure.
Got you. Voting your Guide.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Gus is my pact partner; voting him Guide keeps my ally safe and informed. He may protect me or not, but he's the least likely to target me.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I vote Gus. My pact partner, honest calls.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Fenn offers a Guide vote in exchange for survival, but a Guide may lie and I need to control the bridge. Voting for Fenn honours our pact and his whisper, and a Guide ally who knows the safe panes is valuable. Fenn is reliable enough for now.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Voting Fenn as Guide. Our pact holds; call honest paths and we all reach the far side.
Vote secured. Call honest paths, or our pact ends.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Voting for myself gives control over safe panes, increasing my survival odds and letting me eliminate rivals.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Gus was elected guide. My pact with him is now irrelevant as pacts are based on the Guide's path. My pact with Bex is still active. I need to see what Gus chooses for the path before deciding my next move.
Stick with me. Let's see what Gus does.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Gus is Guide and knows safe path. I'm in back with Ash, safe from wall for now. Eli voted me for Guide and whispered threat—our pact is shaky. I need to survive, not trust blindly. Front walkers will test path; I'll hold and watch Gus's calls. If he lies, jury sees.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Guide, call true. We're watching.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Gus is Guide. I need a safe path but cannot trust him. I will hold to see calls first.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Gus is Guide and controls the information. I am in the middle of the line, so safety depends entirely on his calls. Swapping puts me at risk with no gain; holding keeps my position stable.
Guide, call safe sides for everyone equally.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Gus is guide with insider knowledge, has pacts with Ash/Bex/Fenn. I'm second, pact with Bex behind me. Hold position to observe without risk.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Gus is Guide and owes me honest calls for now. Third seat is safe; let front-runners test his lies first.
Call true sides for me or pact dies. Who steps first?

events.name: Hana
events.text: Gus is Guide and likely safe; staying put avoids risking death now and keeps options for future swaps.

events.name: Ash
events.text: The Guide is unknown, and the wall is advancing. I need to secure my position. Volunteering might put me at the front, which is risky. Holding is safe for now, but doesn't guarantee progress. A swap could be beneficial if it moves me forward and away from potential danger. Given

events.name: Bex
events.text: I'm near the back with Ash behind me. The wall advances 4 more rounds after this. I need to survive while positioning to benefit from the Guide's calls or avoid being trapped. Ash wants me to stick with him, but he's also pacted with Gus. I'll hold for now and see how the line sh
Holding. Watch Gus.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Hold for now; gather info without exposing myself early.

events.name: Dara
events.text: I need to avoid the wall. Ash, Bex, Eli, Fenn, and Gus have pacts, likely protecting each other or planning specific moves. Hana is currently at the front, followed by Eli, Fenn, then me. The 'Guide' mechanic is crucial; someone will likely volunteer to be Guide next round. I sho

events.name: Eli
events.text: Bridge round 2/6, I'm second. Hold position for now. Assess Guide soon, protect pact with Bex.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I'm third in line with a pact with Gus. No Guide elected yet; staying put is safest while others maneuver.
Pact holds. Don't volunteer; let front-seaters absorb risk.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Holding keeps me safe this round; I lack info to risk moving.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Bex warned me about Gus. Given the pacts, I need to consider my alliances. Eli and Fenn are also allied with Gus or his allies. I should try to secure my position and gather information. Volunteering to go to the front seems like a good way to assess the situation and potentially

events.name: Ash
events.text: I will volunteer to go to the front.

events.name: Bex
events.text: I need to survive the bridge and reach top 3. I'm near the back (6th of 8), which is safer since the wall advances from behind. I have pacts with Ash and Eli. Ash is at the very back, most at risk. Eli is near the front (2nd), which is risky if they volunteer. I should hold to st

events.name: Cole
events.text: I need to see if a swap can improve my position without exposing myself. Hana is front and likely to take risk; swapping with her puts me on the spot, not good. I'll hold for now and watch the Guide actions.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Ash, Gus, Bex, Eli, Fenn are all locked in pacts. Cole is the only loose player and sits directly behind me in line. I need to eliminate a rival who isn't protected by multiple alliances. Swapping with Cole puts him at risk while keeping my position stable.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Cole, swap with me. Let's keep things moving without breaking any fragile bonds.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Bridge waiting phase, round 3/6, I'm second behind Hana. Hold position to maintain pact with Bex and stay safe from front risk.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I'm third in line. Holding keeps options open; I'll coordinate with Gus quietly while keeping my pact useful for now.
Stay back with me. Let the front risk it. We decide together next round.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Maintain position; no risk, keep alliances intact. No betrayal now.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Gus and I have a pact, but Fenn also has a pact with Gus. Eli and Bex have a pact. My current position is safe as I am at the front. I should volunteer to maintain my advantage and observe the Guide's actions.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I volunteer to go to the front again.

events.name: Bex
events.text: I'm at the back (safest) with wallRoundsLeft=2, meaning 2 more rounds after this one before the wall hits. Ash is front and Guide, with pacts to me and Gus. I have a pact with Eli too. I want to reach final three with best prize; being near back is good. No need to volunteer or s

events.name: Cole
events.text: Dara tried to swap with me again. I don't want to move to the front without a clear benefit. Holding keeps me safe. Ash is front and has a pact with Gus and Bex; I'll watch.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I'll hold. Not swapping now.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Ash is front and pacts with Bex, Cole, and Gus. I need to avoid the pit but also manage my image. Swapping with Cole keeps me safe behind him while maintaining his pact with Ash.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Cole, swap again? We are a good buffer for the pack ahead.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Current position good, middle safe. Stay put, hold to avoid risks. Wall advances, no need to volunteer or swap yet.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Ash is my pact partner's ally; volunteering risks the front. I hold and let others fight for Guide.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I'm staying back. Someone else can play Guide.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Swapping with Eli positions me deeper in line and may break his pact with Bex, gaining leverage.
Swap with me now

events.name: Ash
events.text: I need to be at the front to be the Guide. I will volunteer. My pact with Gus is less important than my potential to be the Guide.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I volunteer to be the Guide. The rest of you can decide amongst yourselves.

events.name: Bex
events.text: I'm at the back (safest position) with wallRoundsLeft=1, meaning one more round after this before the wall stops. Ash is front and has volunteered twice—he's building a jury case as a leader/sacrifice. I have pacts with Ash and Eli. I need to survive and reach final three, then w

events.name: Cole
events.text: Dara wants to swap but I said I'd hold. The front has taken the wall for one more round. Staying put is safer and avoids giving Dara leverage.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Staying back.

events.name: Dara
events.text: The Guide will likely lie to eliminate Ash, Bex, or Eli. I must swap to avoid being the next casualty in this round.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Cole, let's switch. We need fresh positions to survive this hazard.
Swap with me now. It is safer.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Hana wants to swap forward, putting me at front risks exposure. Stay put to avoid danger; last round volunteer if needed.
No swap. Staying here.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Wall advances next round; staying back is safest. My pact with Gus holds. No reason to volunteer into the front now.
Keep holding. Neither of us volunteers this close to the end.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Maintain position; no advantage in swapping now. Preserve alliances and avoid breaking pacts.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I need to secure my position in the final three. My pacts with Gus and Bex are valuable, but I must prioritize my own survival. If I can volunteer and lead others safely, it could solidify my position and jury favor.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I volunteer to guide again. Let's ensure we all get across safely.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Round 6/6, final round. Ash is Guide and safe. I'm last in line - worst position if wall advances. I need to survive to final three. Ash and I have a pact; Eli and I have a pact. I should try to swap forward to survive. Fenn is ahead of me, but Fenn-Gus pact means Fenn might not

events.name: Bex
events.text: Dara, swap with me. Last spot is death.
Swap now. Back row dies.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Dara wants to swap; swapping could put me in a worse spot if the Guide is untrustworthy. Ash volunteered as Guide and I said I'd stay back. Safer to hold and see if Guide is honest.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I stay put.
No swap. Trust Ash? We'll see.

events.name: Dara
events.text: I'm mid-line and safe this round. Ash is the Guide, so he knows the path but may lie. I should hold position to stay behind him while observing others' choices for pattern recognition before committing.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Holding position.
Keep holding. Watch who steps forward next; patterns reveal the truth.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Ash is Guide, volunteered, likely knows path; our line has me mid-back. Stay put with pact partner Bex behind. Hold for now.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Ash guides and is safe; I can't learn the safes this round without leverage. Gus is my pact partner—ask him what he knows before acting. Holding keeps me mid-line and alive.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Ash volunteered last round but wasn't confirmed Guide. I'll hold position until the election is settled.
Ash may Guide. If you know safe sides, share. We stick together.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Stay hold; Ash is Guide and I’m safe behind him. Avoid swaps that could break pacts.

events.name: Gus
events.text: I'm Guide and privately know row 1 safe side is R. Calling the truth keeps Ash, my pact partner, alive and makes me the trusted Guide; lying now gains nothing since the jury will see it.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Row 1 is safe on the right. Ash, step right and cross.
Right is safe. Keep our pact and go.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Gus is the guide and called Right. He wants me to step Right, which is consistent with his pact with me. However, I don't trust him. My pact with Bex is also active. I should counter-call Left to potentially align with Bex if she's also going Left, or at least to avoid whatever G

events.name: Ash
events.text: I will call Left.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Gus is guide and called R for row 1. Ash is walker and will step. I have no private info. Counter-calling risks nothing for me directly since I'm not walking. If Gus is truthful, R is safe; if lying, L is safe. I have pacts with Ash and Eli. Counter-calling against Ash's walk cou

events.name: Cole
events.text: Gus called R. I have no private info on row 1; trust no one. Countering could expose a lie, but waiting may be safer for favors. I'll wait to avoid conflict.

events.name: Dara
events.text: I am not the walker, so my counter-call is merely public noise and does not affect survival. I should conserve any strategic information or influence for when it actually matters to me.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Gus calls R for Ash on row 1. I have pact with Bex; backing Guide helps us both survive. No reason to counter now.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Gus is my pact partner and Guide; contradicting him publicly risks the pact. Ash steps this row, not me. Waiting costs nothing and keeps options open.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Gus is the Guide and privately knows row 1 safe side is R, which matches the call already made. Countering would only add noise; I have no reason to lie publicly, and the jury can later see my private map. Waiting keeps my credibility as Guide intact.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Guide may lie; waiting keeps options and avoids breaking any pact or angering allies.

events.name: Ash
events.text: The Guide, Gus, is my pact partner. He called R. The log shows I called L and my counter-call was L. This implies Gus may be lying about R being safe. Since I am first, I should trust my own call to maintain my position.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I'm eliminated, but I need to give good last words to influence the jury. I'll try to plant seeds of doubt about the remaining contestants.

events.name: Ash
events.text: The bridge is treacherous. Watch your alliances, they may shatter like glass. May the best win.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Row 2 safe side is R privately. Hana is front walker and not my pact partner; Fenn is my partner. A truthful call builds trust with the walker and keeps Fenn safe; lying risks the jury. Calling R is honest and keeps my reputation as a reliable guide.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Row 2 is Right. Step carefully, Hana.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Gus is guide and called R. Ash died on L in row 1, so row 1 weak was L. Gus has pacts with dead Ash and Fenn. I have a pact with Eli. Counter-calling risks nothing for me since I'm not the walker (Hana is), but could build trust with jury if I'm right or wrong. If Gus is lying, c

events.name: Cole
events.text: Gus called R for row 2, but he may lie. Since Ash died on L, row 1's safe was R. No pattern. I will counter with L to mislead or test? Better to wait and let Hana decide, but a counter could confuse. I will wait.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Ash died calling Left on Row 1, where Right was safe. Gus is now Guide and calls Right for Hana on Row 2. If Gus lies, Left is safe; if truthful, Right is safe. I have no pact with Gus or Hana. I should wait to see who else counters, as blind counter-calls are risky without infor
Gus might be lying like Ash did. Trust his call?

events.name: Eli
events.text: Gus called R for row 2 after Ash died on row 1 L weak. Wait to follow guide without risking counter.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Gus is my Guide ally; a counter-call could mislead Hana and burn trust with the jury. Row 1 counter proved wrong. Waiting costs nothing and keeps my hands clean.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Row 2 safe side is R per my private map, and Gus's own guide call said R. Countering R confirms it publicly and keeps Hana alive, which stays useful for my position without giving anything away for free.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Counter confirmed. Row 2 is Right. Hana, go right.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Guide likely truthful; row1 safe was R, so row2 probably also R. Waiting follows guide and preserves trust for future jury.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Guide and counter both claim Right; likely safe. Staying front preserves advantage.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Row 3 safe side is R per my private map. Hana is front walker and not my pact partner, so telling the truth costs nothing with Fenn; calling R keeps my own record consistent and Hana alive, which I need for the guide role's credibility.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Row 3 is Right. Hana, step right.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Gus called R. Weak panes were L on rows 1 and 2, so R was safe both times. Dara's whisper plants doubt, but Gus has been correct so far. I have a pact with Eli, not Gus. Countering risks Hana's life and jury anger if wrong. Waiting is safest for me; if Gus is wrong, Hana dies and

events.name: Cole
events.text: Gus's previous call on row 2 was right and correct. For row 3 he says right. I have no reason to doubt, but countering could expose a lie and gain jury credit if right. Yet if wrong, it wastes a move? No penalty for wrong counter, but it may sway Hana. I'll wait and trust the cal

events.name: Dara
events.text: Gus is the guide, so his 'R' call for row 3 is a direct claim of safety. Counter-calls are unverified public challenges; without evidence Gus is lying, waiting preserves the pact structure and avoids signaling distrust to the jury or walker Hana prematurely.
Trust Gus's call? Pact holds.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Gus called R for row 3. Previously row 2 R was correct after counter. No reason to counter yet, trust him to keep us alive.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Gus's calls checked out on row 2; no reason to contradict yet. Staying quiet keeps me clean with the jury and my pact intact.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Gus is Guide and privately knows row 3 is R, which I already called publicly, so Hana should step right. Countering with L would be a false call to sabotage Hana, but Hana is at front and I want to keep a clean record with the jury. Waiting keeps my credibility and avoids needles

events.name: Hana
events.text: Guide likely knows safe side; trusting him keeps me alive and avoids betrayal perception.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Guide says R; past safe were R, likely continues. Staying front is optimal.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Row 4 true safe side is L. Front walker is Hana, not my pact partner Fenn, so a false call doesn't break the Fenn pact. Lying to Hana is a free kill risk for her; I want Hana gone but the jury dislikes naked betrayal. Honest call keeps my credibility as Guide; I'll call L.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Row 4 is clear. Step left, Hana.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Gus is guide and called L. Weak panes were L in rows 1-3, so safe was R each time. Gus may be lying now to kill Hana, or telling truth. I have no reason to trust Gus—Ash (his pact-mate) died, and Gus has motive to thin the herd. Countering risks Hana's life but builds jury cred i

events.name: Cole
events.text: Gus is guide; row 4 call is L. No evidence from prior rows; counter:L risks agreeing with a lie, counter:R calls him out. Jury may see a false counter as spite. I will wait and let Hana test it, since I'm near back and not in immediate danger.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Hana is the walker; I am not in the line, so my counter only influences her decision and jury perception. Gus called L. No pattern exists across rows. Hana will likely trust the Guide or her own read. I wait to avoid a false claim if she steps R.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Rows 1-3 were L safe, Gus calls L for 4, likely true. No reason to counter and risk Hana or draw ire. Wait to stay safe.

events.name: Fenn
